title: Ancient Puzzle
transcript: This is the oldest chess puzzle ever found, composed in 836 AD. And I am going to explain it to you on a super modern smart board. If it was black to move, white would be completely lost in just one move. This would be a checkmate. But that is not the case, and we can notice that the black king is actually quite restricted by the white pieces. So the first move aims at opening up this rook by sacrificing the knight with knight to A5 check. There is nowhere for this king to go. So the black rook has to accept the sacrifice of the knight. And now it seems like there is no safe check to give with either this rook or this rook. Both of these squares are defended by the king. But that is the key to solving this puzzle. You see the king is also surrounded by our king and by this pawn. So what we want to do is to actually sacrifice more material by taking the knight with a check. The only move available for black is to take the rook. And now we have lured this king into a sandwich between the white king and the pawn, but also the two black pieces taking away these important squares. And so incredibly, with only one rook left, rook to D6 is checkmate. If you like this board, read the caption.
